metaDescription: Six under-counter ice makers compared on drain method, bin size, daily output, width and whether a gravity drain, a pump or no drain suits your install.
expertTake: The Euhomy 100 lb under-counter maker with a drain pump is the pick for most homes, because the pump lets you install it where a gravity drain will not reach. The Mojgar drainless unit is the choice when no drain exists at all. Skip the biggest machines for a home bar unless you entertain constantly, because a 24 lb bin is the real limit and a 130 lb rating cannot change that.
introParagraphs: An under-counter ice maker is a built-in appliance: a small cabinet that fits under a counter, makes ice in a tray, drops it into a bin and holds it cold. It replaces bags of ice and the freezer space they steal, and it works silently in the background once it is installed.

The installation question comes first. Some models drain by gravity into a pipe below the machine, some include a pump that lifts the meltwater to a higher drain, and a few skip the drain entirely. After that come bin size, width and the quality of the ice, and we rank the machines on those points.

products.name: Euhomy under-counter ice maker with drain pump, 100 lb per day, 24 lb bin

specList.label: Daily output
specList.value: Up to 100 lb of clear ice

products.description:
The drain pump is what makes this Euhomy the most installable under-counter machine in the group. A standard unit relies on gravity, which means the drain has to sit below the machine, and in many kitchens and basements it does not. A pump lifts the meltwater to a higher drain, so the machine can go where you want it.

It makes up to 100 pounds of clear ice a day and stores 24 pounds in a built-in bin, in a compact cabinet about 15 inches wide, 18.5 deep and 34 tall including legs. It can be built in or stand alone. Clear cubes melt slowly and look good in a glass.

Versus the Euhomy 90 lb gravity model it adds a pump and 10 more pounds of daily output. Clean the pump's filter, sanitize the bin and descale the water system on a schedule.
products.bestFor: Most homes where a gravity drain will not reach.
pros: Drain pump lifts meltwater to a higher drain
Up to 100 lb of clear ice per day
cons: 24 lb bin limits a large party
A pump is one more part that can fail

products.name: Euhomy 15 inch under-counter ice maker, 90 lb per day, 24 lb bin, gravity drainage
products.description:
A gravity drain is the simplest arrangement when it is available: the meltwater runs down a pipe, with no pump to maintain. This Euhomy makes 90 pounds a day at about 40 cubes per cycle and holds 24 pounds, with three ice sizes selectable on an LCD panel.

The maker pitches it for busy service, saying the output keeps hundreds of drinks flowing through a rush. The LCD shows ice-full and water status, and a self-cleaning function covers routine flushing. The 15 inch width fits standard cabinet gaps.

Compared with the 100 lb pump model it has no pump and a slightly lower output. Confirm that your drain sits below the machine before buying, sanitize the bin on a schedule and descale the water system.
products.bestFor: Kitchens with a drain below the machine.
pros: 90 lb per day, about 40 cubes per cycle
cons: Needs a drain below the machine
24 lb bin is modest for large gatherings

products.name: Mojgar drainless under-counter ice maker, 25 lb per day, 22 lb bin, crescent ice
products.description:
A drainless design is the only way to put an ice maker where there is no drain at all, and the Mojgar is built for that: no drain run, so installation is a matter of power, water supply and a spot. It makes 25 pounds a day and stores 22 pounds, with smooth crescent ice that melts slowly.

The trade is output. At 25 pounds a day it is a fraction of the 90 to 130 pound machines, so it suits a household or a small office, not a bar. A reversible door lets you hang it to suit the room. The meltwater is managed inside the cabinet, which is why the output is lower.

Beside the Euhomy units it needs far less plumbing. Sanitize the bin, descale the water system and clear the vents on a schedule.
products.bestFor: Spots with no drain, such as a closet bar or a basement corner.
pros: 22 lb bin with 25 lb per day

products.name: ICEPURE 15 inch under-counter ice maker with drain pump and filter, 90 lb, WiFi
products.description:
A drain pump, a water filter and WiFi control with a 24-hour timer make this ICEPURE the connected option. It makes 90 pounds a day at 40 cubes per cycle, with a cycle time of 10 to 18 minutes, and stores 26 pounds, slightly more than the Euhomy units.

The app lets you adjust ice thickness, start and stop remotely and schedule production, and a smart reminder prompts you about maintenance. That reminder is useful, because under-counter machines are easy to forget. The maker also positions the compact 15 inch body for RVs, bars and small businesses.

Against the Euhomy pump model it adds smart features and a larger bin. Keep the filter fresh, sanitize the bin and descale on schedule.
products.bestFor: Owners who want scheduling, reminders and a pump drain.
pros: Drain pump and a built-in water filter
WiFi remote control and a 24 hour timer
26 lb bin and 90 lb per day
cons: Cycle time ranges from 10 to 18 minutes

products.name: Coolake under-counter ice maker, 120 lb per day, 40 lb bin, outdoor built-in

specList.label: Daily output
specList.value: Up to 120 lb of clear ice

products.description:
Positioned for outdoor bars and kitchens as well as indoor ones, this Coolake combines the highest output in the guide, up to 120 pounds a day, with a 40 pound bin, the biggest here. For an outdoor kitchen where entertaining is the whole point, that reserve matters.

A one-touch self-cleaning function and an LCD panel that adjusts cube thickness make the interface easy. Outdoor use raises the stakes: heat cuts output, and dust and insects get into everything. Clear cubes melt slowly, which suits hot weather.

Compared with the Euhomy units it has a larger bin and output at a larger size. Shade the machine, clear the vents often and sanitize the bin on a schedule.
products.bestFor: Outdoor kitchens and big entertaining spaces.
pros: 40 lb bin is the largest here
cons: Heat and dust affect an outdoor machine
Larger and costlier than the 15 inch units

products.name: Whynter UIM-155 built-in stainless steel ice maker, under-counter, 12 lb per day, no drain

specList.label: Daily output
specList.value: Up to 12 lb of crescent ice

products.description:
A drain-free, front-venting under-counter machine is the Whynter's calling card: it fits into a cabinet run with no side or rear clearance and no drain. It makes 12 pounds of crescent-shaped cubes in 24 hours, a low output that matches a small home bar or a wine cellar.

The low output is the honest limit, since 12 pounds a day is about a third of a countertop nugget maker. Its virtue is simplicity of installation and a tidy stainless look. A cabinet that vents through the front means it will not overheat a closed cabinet.

Compared with the Mojgar drainless unit it makes about half as much. Sanitize the bin, descale and keep the front grille clear.
products.bestFor: Small home bars where a trickle of ice is enough.
pros: Front venting needs no side clearance
cons: 12 lb per day is very low

buyingCriteria.explanation: A gravity drain needs a drain below the machine, like the Euhomy 90 lb. A drain pump, like the Euhomy 100 lb and the ICEPURE, lifts meltwater to a higher drain. A drainless design, like the Mojgar and the Whynter, needs no drain but makes far less ice. The install location decides this first. A plumber can add a drain, but that cost often exceeds the price difference between a gravity unit and a pump unit, so check the drain before you fall in love with a model.

Under-counter bins hold 22 to 40 pounds, and a 24 pound bin is the common figure. The Coolake's 40 pound bin is the largest. A machine rated at 100 pounds a day with a 24 pound bin is a trickle charger: it refills the bin through the evening, but a rush drains it. Match the bin to your peak. Count the drinks you serve in your busiest hour, assume a pound of ice for every three or four drinks and check that the bin can cover that hour with a margin.

Ratings run from 12 pounds on the Whynter to 120 on the Coolake, at cool conditions. A hot garage or an outdoor kitchen cuts output sharply. The Euhomy and ICEPURE quote around 40 cubes per cycle, which is the number that shows the evaporator size.

The Euhomy and ICEPURE units are about 15 inches wide, a standard cabinet gap. The Whynter's front venting avoids side and rear clearance. Measure the opening, the height with legs and the space for the drain line before you buy. Also check which way the door swings and whether the front grille has room to breathe, since a machine that cannot vent will run hot and make less ice.

An LCD panel that adjusts ice thickness, as on the Euhomy, Coolake and ICEPURE, lets you tune the ice. Wi-Fi and a timer on the ICEPURE help scheduling and reminders. Simple machines have fewer parts to fail. Choose features only if you will use them.

Scale and slime are the long-term enemies of an under-counter machine. A built-in filter, as on the ICEPURE, helps, and every unit needs the bin sanitized and the water system descaled on a schedule. A machine tucked under a counter is easy to forget, so set reminders.

howWeEvaluated.title: Install flexibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared gravity, pump and drainless designs, giving credit to the pump models for placement flexibility. A drainless unit scored for no-drain spots. We noted the output cost of drainless design.

howWeEvaluated.title: Bin and output
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at bins from 22 to 40 pounds and output from 12 to 120 pounds. A balanced pair scored best. A high output with a small bin was marked as a trickle charger.

howWeEvaluated.title: Width and clearance
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered 15 inch widths and front venting. Machines that fit a standard cabinet gap scored higher. We noted the height with legs.

howWeEvaluated.title: Controls and filters
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at LCD panels, Wi-Fi, timers and the ICEPURE's built-in filter. Features that support maintenance scored higher. Simple units scored for reliability.

howWeEvaluated.title: Outdoor and heat
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted the Coolake's outdoor positioning and the effect of heat on output. A machine in the sun makes less ice. We weighed shade and ventilation needs.

cards.label: Pump or gravity
cards.text: The Euhomy and ICEPURE machines make 90 to 100 pounds a day and need a drain, either below the machine or lifted by a pump.

cards.label: Drainless
cards.text: The Mojgar and Whynter need no drain but make only 12 to 25 pounds a day.

howToChoose.note: Choose by what your install allows, then by how much ice you need.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: An outdoor-rated machine, shade, ventilation and a larger bin to cover heat-driven drops in output.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Coolake is positioned for outdoor built-in use with a 40 lb bin and 120 lb daily rating.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You entertain often or need a pump drain. The Coolake, the Euhomy 100 lb and the ICEPURE repay.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You want modest ice in a small bar. The Whynter or Mojgar is enough.

maintenance.why: A warm, wet bin grows slime. Use an approved sanitizer and rinse well.
Scale coats the evaporator and cuts output. Use a maker-approved descaler and rinse thoroughly.

maintenance.task: Clean the pump filter and drain line
maintenance.why: A clogged pump or drain floods the bin. Pour water through to confirm flow.
A clogged filter cuts flow and lets minerals through. Keep a spare on hand.
Dust blocks heat rejection, especially in a garage or outdoors. A brush keeps output up, and a quick look at the grille each month tells you whether the machine is breathing.

faq.q: Do under-counter ice makers need a drain?
faq.a: Most do, either a gravity drain below the machine or a pump to a higher drain. Drainless models like the Mojgar and the Whynter need none but make far less ice.

faq.q: How much ice do I really need?
faq.a: Bin size matters more than daily output for entertaining. A 24 pound bin holds enough for a small party, and the machine refills it slowly through the evening. For a bigger party, start the day early so the bin is full, and keep a cooler of bagged ice as a backup for the busiest hour.

Only models rated for it, like the Coolake. Heat cuts output and dust and insects need keeping out, so shade and clear vents are important. An outdoor machine also needs a power outlet on a protected circuit and a water line that will not freeze, and in cold climates the machine should be drained and covered for winter.

faq.q: What is a drain pump for?
faq.a: It lifts meltwater to a drain higher than the machine, so you can install it where a gravity drain will not reach. It is one more part to maintain. The pump has a small filter that clogs with scale, so clean it on schedule, and make sure the discharge hose rises and falls without kinks, since a kinked hose makes the pump labor and fail early.

faq.q: How often should I clean it?
faq.a: Sanitize the bin monthly, descale every few months and check the drain or pump filter. A calendar reminder or a smart alert helps. An under-counter machine sits behind a cabinet door and out of sight, which is exactly why it gets forgotten, so tie the routine to something you already do monthly.

faq.q: Can I leave the ice in the bin?
faq.a: Yes. The bin is insulated and keeps ice cold, though some melting occurs and meltwater drains away or recirculates. Rotate the ice if it sits for days. Ice that has sat for a week can pick up freezer-like odors and clump, so scoop out and discard the old bottom layer now and then and let the machine make a fresh supply.
